report: Freshly inspected the current start output: the complete claim, whole semantic_spec.rs implementation context, its complete selected modules_parse_recovery_completeness test, and the full association inventory. Empty represented sets are covered by the same prohibition as sets retaining safe siblings. These are not established by assertions in the current evidence. The implementation TODO explicitly states that uniform question-sensitive completeness is not implemented despite retained parse errors. This is an honest deferral of the missing consumer-facing completeness mechanism, not a claim that retaining errors alone satisfies the contract. The sole test has comments and no executable assertions. Its proposed malformed and unsupported-item fixtures, safe sibling retention, and refusal of downstream false negatives describe necessary future coverage, not completed verification. Its prerequisite is the missing completeness propagation mechanism identified directly above it. Once implemented, verification must distinguish error items from error CST nodes, terminal recovery from exhaustive semantic completion, empty from nonempty retained sets, and relevant errors from proven irrelevant errors. All these aspects remain deferred by the current TODO evidence. No production implementation was supplied or relied upon as completed behavior, and no helper calls exist in this empty test to follow. The captured meta.reviews.decisions policy permits accepting adequately explained explicit TODO gaps without relabeling them. The current implementation and test TODOs identify the substantive missing mechanism and its verification matrix sufficiently for that acceptance; no source edits are required for this review.
